cards.back: Introduction: name the production, company, venue, date and the production's overall intention.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Writing a Theatre Review
cards.back: SEE framework: State the technique, Evidence from the production, Effect on the audience — use for every analytical point.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Writing a Theatre Review
cards.back: Analysis paragraphs: focus on one aspect per paragraph (e.g. performance, then design, then direction).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Writing a Theatre Review
cards.back: Conclusion: evaluate the overall effectiveness — did the production achieve its intention? Sum up your judgement.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Writing a Theatre Review
cards.back: Analytical style: precise terminology, specific moments, supported judgements — never vague or subjective language.

cards.front: What should you know about drama exam tips?
cards.back: Time management for Section B (live theatre): 5 minutes planning (which moments will you write about?), 30 minutes writing (structured paragraphs using SEE), 5 minutes checking (terminology, evidence, judgements). Plan your key moments BEFORE you start writing to ensure you have enough material.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: A theatre review should start with your overall opinion and then give reasons why you liked or disliked the show. Correct: A theatre review should start with FACTUAL CONTEXT (production, company, venue, intention) and then provide ANALYSIS and EVALUATION of specific choices. Write a structured theatre review of a production you have seen, evaluating the effectiveness of the performance and design choices.

The live theatre review (Component 1 Section B) assesses AO2 (20%). The question asks you to analyse and evaluate a production you have seen. You must: name the production, analyse specific performance and design choices, evaluate their effectiveness, and use precise terminology. cards.front: Structure and Content of a Theatre Review
cards.back: A GCSE theatre review must be structured, analytical and evaluative, quite different from a subjective personal response. The review should open with a brief contextual introduction (production title, theatre, director, date), then analyse specific aspects of the production in organised paragraphs, and conclude with an overall evaluation of the production's effectiveness.
